donor.note: Same publisher's Windows port of the same engine build, already installable (32/33 sites, confidence 1.0, resolved directly from this binary's own native namespace-qualified symbols). Used here as the match source instead of a cross-platform donor.

matcher_calibration.note: The already-published calibration in data/adjudication/METHOD.md section 1 (run v1 sourced from binary 22 into binary 19, a fully-named Mac donor) applies directly here, since the source side and matching technique are identical -- only the destination differs. margin 0.15-0.30 -> ~85-91% loose agreement, margin 0.30+ -> ~89% loose agreement, margin 0.000 -> ~9-10% agreement (untrustworthy). A fresh self-calibration against binary 23's own native names was attempted but is not viable: only 128 of 26965 functions carry name_origin='namespace' (a real symbol), and none are game-engine classes -- they are MSVC STL/MFC/ATL/Concurrency-Runtime symbols pulled in from the runtime library, not NWScript VM code. binary 23 has no locally-verifiable ground truth of its own for the classes this table needs.

accept_rule: Same as METHOD.md: accept requires at least two independent signals, at least one of which is not run v1 (shape/size/n_blocks/n_callees comparison against the known-good binary 22 site, or a distinguishing instruction pattern read directly from the binary). A calibrated-trustworthy match margin alone is not sufficient.
counts_note: All 12 required VM/stack sites now accepted (7 from the original pass, 5 more -- StackPopInteger, StackPushInteger, StackPopFloat, StackPopObject, StackPushObject -- from resolving the degenerate cluster below), plus 4 bonus optional sites (StackPopVector, StackPushVector, StackPopEngineStructure, StackPushEngineStructure) resolved by the same method. The cluster that blocked installability in the original pass turned out to be a single 14-function translation-unit block, byte-for-byte size-identical to donor binary 22's own copy of the same block at every position, with a uniform +1 positional offset explained exactly by one extra leading function (SetCommandImplementer) that is not one of this project's tracked hook sites. TU-layout isomorphism: donor binary 22 has a 14-function consecutive block at 0x640ba0-0x640d50 (SetCommandImplementer, StackPopInteger, StackPushInteger, StackPopFloat, StackPushFloat, StackPopVector, StackPushVector, StackPopString, StackPushString, StackPopEngineStructure, StackPushEngineStructure, StackPopObject, StackPushObject, StackPopCommand -- all 14 individually named in the corpus, since binary 22 is fully resolved). Binary 23's cluster has 13 thunks at 0x6fd980-0x6fdb10, one short of the donor's 14 -- StackPopCommand (donor position 14, the last of the block) has no counterpart inside this span in binary 23, consistent with the accepted sites below stopping at StackPushObject. Positions 2-13 in binary 23 map to donor positions 1-12 (StackPopInteger through StackPushObject) with a uniform +1 offset, which the three already-accepted sites in this file (StackPushFloat at binary-23 position 5, StackPopString at position 8, StackPushString at position 9) already confirmed independently before this pass. Binary 23 position 1 (0x6fd980) is therefore SetCommandImplementer's counterpart -- not one of this project's tracked hook sites, so it is not emitted as a binding, but its presence and exact size match (28=28) is what explains and confirms the +1 offset rather than leaving it as an unexplained coincidence.
